questions: Did s-bend and slalom max_error fall below 0.061 m, or did those runs progress further before going off track?
Did line_loss_events stay at 0 on all three tracks with mass 0.6 kg?
Did oval progress hold near 0.7, and did the oval finish return? If oval progress fell below 0.5, that is the revert trigger.
Did oval steering_oscillation stay at or below 0.33, or did the lighter robot overshoot?
On the drift cases, does the controller now correct earlier at the edge, or does it still reach 0.06 m at the same bend?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If oval progress falls below 0.5, revert mass to 0.8 kg, since iteration 5 is the best measured geometry. If s-bend and slalom still reach 0.061 m with losses at 0, report which bend is the tightest drift point so the next test can target it. Do not retry inner ±0.04 m, sensor_size 0.016 m, wheel_track 0.10 m or y 0.06 m, since all were rejected in iterations 3, 4, 6 and 7.

intent: Return to the iteration 5 geometry, the best measured so far (151.9), and change one variable: total mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. Sensor layout (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, y 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints), wheel_track 0.12 m and wheel_radius 0.03 m stay fixed, so any change in drift or progress comes from the lower yaw inertia.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that moving the inner sensors to ±0.04 m cut oval progress to 0.22 and brought back line losses on s-bend and slalom (1.0 per run), so the inner spacing stays at ±0.03 m. The Integrator's feedback for this iteration was written before the iteration 7 race and recommended re-testing the inner ±0.04 m spacing, which is now stale. The remaining failure at iteration 5 is edge drift with losses at 0, so this iteration tests whether lower mass (lower yaw inertia) gives a quicker correction without changing the sensor layout.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (inner sensors moved to ±0.04 m at 12 mm, outer ±0.06 m, y 0.04 m, 12 cm track) scored 59.0, well below iteration 5's 151.9. Oval progress fell from 0.71 to 0.22, oval line losses rose to 1.9 per run, and s-bend and slalom losses returned to 1.0 per run. The inner ±0.04 m spacing is therefore rejected. The Robot Integrator's pre-agreed revert rule applies here (oval progress below 0.5 means return the inner sensors to ±0.03 m).

The Integrator's current feedback (entityR1) was written for the iteration 8 candidate before it raced. It recommends testing the inner ±0.04 m spacing again, which iteration 7 has already run and rejected. I have therefore treated that feedback as stale on that point and not as a reason to repeat the test.

Iteration 5 remains the best measured geometry: outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, y 0.04 m, 12 cm track, 0.8 kg. Its s-bend and slalom line losses are 0.0, and every run ends at the 0.06 m edge with max_error about 0.061 m, so the remaining failure is edge drift on the line, not tape loss. The 16 mm footprint (iteration 6) and the inner ±0.04 m spacing both cut oval progress, and the 0.10 m track and y 0.06 m (iterations 3 and 4) did too. All of these are rejected.

The untested lever that does not touch the sensor layout, the footprint or the track is body mass. Yaw inertia is mass × (body_length² + body_width²)/12, so reducing mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg lowers the inertia the robot must overcome to turn. A quicker turn response should let the robot correct sooner when it drifts toward the 0.06 m edge on s-bend and slalom, while the sensor layout that removed losses is kept. The off-track limit does not change with mass. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.061 m, or those runs progressing further, with line losses still at 0 and oval progress holding near 0.7. The risk is that a lighter robot overshoots or changes the oval response, so if oval progress falls below 0.5, the next step is to revert mass to 0.8 kg.
